title: DevX docs scratch journal — SDK quick fixes & sample apps
content:
Quick context: sprint bleed-over; half-day heads-down on sample apps + gap doc. This is a personal scratchpad for small doc updates, code snippets, and micro-tasks I want to finish before demo. Not polished — just enough to copy into PRs.

Top priorities (short):
- Quickstart: add streaming + function-call minimal example (must be < 15 lines)
- Sample app: react-chat-widget MVP + serverless example using Redwood Hosted edge endpoint
- FAQ: clarify Dedicated vs Hosted routing policy example (cost vs latency table)
- Snippets: batching config + prefix cache example for JS and Python SDKs

Today (2026-03-05):
- 09:30 — Sync with Marcus: agreed streaming snippet should show partial tokens + cancellation. Marcus will add test harness.
- 10:45 — Drafted streaming snippet (below). Need to factor into quickstart and examples/streaming.md.
- 13:00 — Pair with Sofia on sample app routing logic. Decided to use two-code-path README (hosted vs dedicated).
- 15:20 — Opened PR to add errors section to quickstart (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/342

Streaming snippet (JS, minimal):
// pseudocode for docs, keep small
const res = await client.stream({ model: 'redwood-4k', input: 'Summarize this...' });
for await (const chunk of res) {
  // update UI with chunk.token_text
}
// show cancel example:
controller.abort();

Doc gaps I keep hitting (notes for editorial pass):
- No short example demonstrating function/tool calling with streaming + structured JSON output. Many users ask how to wire tool calls in streaming flows.
- Missing explicit error codes mapping for common client-side failures (rate_limit, model_unavailable, auth) + remediation steps.
- No single place that contrasts "pin model version" vs "model alias with rollout" for Dedicated customers — need a tiny diagram + migration steps.
- Batching config examples are only in Python; need JS + pseudocode showing max_batch_size, max_latency_ms, and when to choose disabled batching.

Sample app TODOs (concrete):
- react-chat-widget:
  - create repo scaffold (src/, public/, README with quickstart) — TODO by EOD 2026-03-09
  - add streaming UI (optimistic render of tokens) + cancel button
  - button to switch route: hosted vs dedicated (toggle) — show cost estimate per request
- serverless-proxy: minimal edge lambda that forwards requests and injects routing headers. Include example of fallbacks when dedicated capacity is exhausted.

UX copy quick wins:
- Quickstart first paragraph: replace "simple API" with "predictable latency API with streaming" — highlight both.
- Error section: add a small callout on transient 503s and automatic fallback to smaller model.
- Example header: rename "Basic usage" -> "Quickstart (2 min)" and move advanced topics down.

Open questions / blockers:
- How to document the cost tradeoff for streaming vs non-streaming on token billing? Need finance to confirm wording. (Pinged Nora in #pricing).
- Do we have metrics on how often customers use function calling + streaming together? Not sure — asked Data team for query.
- Need maintainers for JS SDK examples — Marcus volunteered but bandwidth is tight. Might move some to community contributions.

Short checklist before merging PRs:
- [ ] Add streaming snippet to quickstart + examples/streaming.md
- [ ] Add function-calling streaming mini-example in examples/functions.md
- [ ] Add batching JS snippets to examples/batching.md
- [ ] Cross-link quickstart to Console rollouts docs (product)
- [ ] Get sign-off from Marcus on token/cost wording

Handy copy bits (paste-ready):
- Quickstart blurb: "Use our SDK to stream token-by-token responses for low-latency UIs. Cancel at any time and only pay for generated tokens."
- Error remediation blurb: "If you receive RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, consider using a backoff + jitter strategy; for critical flows, add a retry with a smaller model alias as fallback."

Notes to self:
- When updating examples, try to keep them under 50 LOC so they live in README and can be copy-pasted.
- Add a tiny test (playwright unit) that verifies streaming UI receives tokens in order. Put in sdk/examples/tests/stream.spec.ts

Follow-ups scheduled:
- 2026-03-07: review PR for streaming snippet with Marcus
- 2026-03-09: create initial react-chat-widget repo + seed README
- 2026-03-11: compile editorial pass and send to product for review

Random TODO (low priority):
- Add a tiny cheat-sheet: "Which SDK example to use when" mapping (Quickstart / Streaming / Functions / Embeddings)

End of scratch notes. Will convert into a tidy PR description before pushing.

-- Aisha
